author: hoeschec
text:
I am going to post a few drawings I have regarding swap zones - I am learning how important they are in identifying original supply/demand zones (as opposed to RBD/DBR reactions to the original supply/demand zones).

Quote: "When an opposite transaction of orders execute then price is likely to reach those orders to make LQ, this is why IF says: FOs never happen by chance" - Salivan & IF

Opposite transaction of orders = swap zone

Sellers in control, swaps to buyers in control buyers in control swaps to sellers in control

Not all swap zones are created equal, and there isn't much in Marketpedia on identifying these zones, so I want to post a few drawings to get a better idea of which swap zones are the strongest.

Question # 1: We want to pick swap zones that have kept price down (or held price up). Untested swap zones aren't proven yet so we can't discern the strength of the order flow. FTR's that hold price down one or several times has strong order flow -engulfing that swap zone would be significant. Would we say that good swap zones are also ORFL's?

Drawing:

Question # 2: When we say "holds price up/holds price down" what does that mean? Does it mean price returns to the FTR on its FTB, bounces, and makes a new high/low? Price can return to the FTR on its FTB and bounce, but not create a new high or low...that would indicate the FTR had decent order flow but not substantial enough to push price to a new high/low. We would see an engulf of this FTR as somewhat important but not nearly as important as an engulf of a FTR that held price & price made a new low/high as a result of the bounce.

Drawing:

Salivan often uses the ORFL concept in his trading. If an engulf of a swap zone occurs and the new FTR/FL that is formed (new order flow) is tested by price (FTB to the FTR) we would ID this as a ORFL. We know the FTR/FL that proceeds an engulf of a swap zone is true supply/demand and is also the target for future shorts/longs.

We would expect a deep RT to occur before the target is hit..right?

Hi Kutumbaba,

I don't use PAZ as much as I should...to me, a PAZ is the space between FTR's or an area of compressed PA (FTR's that have all been visited by price to the MPL..leaving no more order flow. The significance of a PAZ (to me) is PAZ = lack of order flow. It is 'dead space' where price moves between two FL's. When price breaks a level and pierces a PAZ, I interpret that move as an engulf.

Of course, due to fractals, there are always PAZ within PAZ within PAZ etc... as we step down in the time frame. This complicates it a bit

I appreciate your post because I have limited understanding of a PAZ, and want to learn more. I've been wanting to read up on Les Paul's Journal to see how he incorporated the PAZ in his trading. I am sure there is a lot of detail I've yet to uncover.

Lately, my motto has been 'simplicity'. I must train my brain to see only the important price structures in a chart, and be able to discern these important price structures-while incorporating the issue of scale.

I like your analogy of a 'compass'. Just last night, I wrote notes down on my computer to post about this. To me, the engulf is the true compass, as it keeps us focused on the big picture. I think this has a lot to do with learning how to trade in different scales. I am currently going back through Salivan's top down analysis on Post # 552 (Art of War Journal)

www.readthemarket.com/index.php/forum/jo...art-of-war?start=550

His top down analysis starts with a HTF upside engulf in to a PAZ. The rest of his analysis is amazing, but his focus was to find the optimal place to get long. Ultimately, he was looking for a place to get long because of the engulf in the HTF charts. If the HTF engulf acts as our compass, we can mitigate the confusion and complication of scale. I will be posting more about this once I have a better understanding myself.

Jurij also mentioned the issue of scale in his journal (see his post # 398) www.readthemarket.com/index.php/forum/jo...j-s-corner?start=375 It sounds like he may also be discovering more about trading with scale.

Please feel free to post anything you feel is relevant regarding the PAZ in my journal. I always appreciate the help, and I'm sure there are many traders reading through these journals who will also find the information useful.

author: hoeschec
text:
I've been practicing lately on understanding scale. Here are some quick notes about my findings so far:

This is conceptual....I will be posting charts as I become more comfortable with the basics.

Price begins a new move by engulfing a swap zone. A FTR usually forms after an engulf and this zone is:

1. True supply/demand 2. FTR/FL 3. MPL 4. Origin of the move up/down 5. Target for future buys/sells

This is true regardless of the scale. 1 minute chart or monthly chart...the structure and fluidity of how price moves does not change. It is the dynamic behind how orders are filled and how price moves. PA doesn't exist because we say it does, or because we name the individual components. PA forms the formations we see because that is how price moves...

Analogy: we've all heard the comparison that the market is like a Russian 'nesting doll' (also referred to as Matryoshka Doll). It is a good analogy. Each smaller scale is nested in with the higher time frame that proceeds it. The higher the time frame, the more data is included (even if it is hard to see). We often have to drop down to lower time frames to see the details of PA on lower time frames. Every engulf/FTR/FL/PAZ/target/MPL etc.... exists in various scales within the market.

As with the market, each smaller doll fits inside of a bigger doll.

Assume all the dolls are put together: Even though you can't see all the individual dolls when they are assembled together, you know all the individual dolls exists within the largest doll. You also know (regardless of what size the doll is) the following:

1. Every doll has a head

2. Every doll has two eyes

3. Every doll has two arms

4. Every doll is painted and made of the same material etc...

5. ** You can't properly put the dolls all together without starting with the smallest doll and placing larger dolls over it consecutively. The entire doll's assemblage requires all dolls to work together** ( I am not suggesting you always start a top-down analysis by beginning on a 1-min chart, but I use this example to emphasize each part's contribution to the 'whole'. The smallest doll gets put away first, the largest doll gets assembled last (over the top of all the smaller dolls)

Similar to a Russian doll, the market has its version of heads, eyes, arms, etc...Each time new orders are transacted (regardless of scale), we have a new 'doll' with fresh order flow.

We know this following is also true:

1. Price engulfs to indicate future directional flow of price

2. FTR/FL formed after important engulfs are origins and future targets

3. Every engulf has a target - regardless of which scale it forms on

4. Engulfs are valid and important until its target is hit.

5. The MPL is important as last place of free order flow until price fakes out to consume the orders

6. You have to pay close attention to all time frames, at all times.

More to follow in next post...

author: hoeschec
text:
(Continuation of post above)

Here is AUD-USD Daily Chart:

I labeled the chart according to which zones were the largest, and which were smaller. There are many smaller zones located to the right of 'Medium Doll B'.

Notice that every RBD has an engulf of its own - and an associated Origin and TG for shorts. These engulfs are valid and so are the targets...it just so happens that they are occurring within the large origin/target (PAZ) of the main original zone (labeled as "Bigger Doll A")

As price bounces around in the large PAZ created between the two FL's (and two origins) of 'bigger doll A', it forms numerous RBD reactions. Each of these RBD reactions that their own engulfs, fakeouts, and origins/targets. Each of these RBD's have PAZ too.

Salivan took the AUD-USD short trade last week, and if you refer to his chart, he writes " last pocket of demand is consumed"...this happened after a confirmed downside engulf. (you can see the chart on his journal post # 692). That demand pocket was medium time frame origin 'up' and the future target for shorts. The shorts that pushed price in to the zone consumed the buy orders...clearing the way for price to drop down to the next target of 'Medium Doll B'. The smaller time frame targets have to be cleared before price can be free to move down and hit the original target for shorts - which originated at 'Bigger Doll A".

Once a target is hit, the engulf that preceded the target is satisfied, and price can move on to take out the next closest target... once that target is hit, price can drop to the next largest target etc... Price will satisfy all the lower time frame engulfs/targets first because they have to....these smaller targets/origins were formed inside the HTF PAZ.

I think this is how you can keep track of price on multiple time frames- know all of the EG's and Targets and identify them as they become satisfied. Always know where your main PAZ is located.

as always, I could be wrong about this, so please don't take this as 100% true until an associate or master trader agrees

)
